A user reports a bug. Where do you look?

Start from the symptom, not from your favorite panel

Browser DevTools mastery (used in every phase) · 2/5

Each panel records one kind of evidence

  1. 1Network: every request and its timing phases
  2. 2Performance: main-thread tasks on a timeline
  3. 3Memory: what the JavaScript heap holds
  4. 4Elements: the DOM and the CSS rules that apply
  5. 5Application: service workers, caches and storage

Browser DevTools mastery (used in every phase) · 3/5

Symptoms of speed and memory

  1. 1The first load is slow
  2. 2Clicks and scrolling feel slow
  3. 3The tab gets slower the longer it is open
Slow first load
Slow clicks
Memory grows

Browser DevTools mastery (used in every phase) · 4/5

Symptoms of a wrong result

  1. 1The layout is broken
  2. 2Users see old data after a deploy
  3. 3An error happens only on an iPhone
Broken layout
Stale data
Error only on iPhone

Browser DevTools mastery (used in every phase) · 5/5

The triage rule

  1. 1Write the symptom in one sentence
  2. 2Open the panel that records that evidence
  3. 3Reproduce the problem while it records
  4. 4Change code only after the evidence names a cause

Deep dive: Slow first load

Open Network and read the Timing tab

  1. 1Tick Disable cache: you load like a first-time visitor
  2. 2Throttle to Slow 4G and reload
  3. 3Open the slowest request, then its Timing tab
  4. 4Long Waiting (TTFB): look at the server
  5. 5Long Content Download: look at file size

Press Previous (‹ or the left arrow key) to return to the main path.

Deep dive: Slow first load

Wrong first choice: Memory

Network first

  • One row per request
  • Time split into phases
  • Points to server or file size

Memory first

  • Heap objects and sizes
  • No request timing
  • The slow request stays hidden

A slow load is a request problem until the Timing tab says otherwise.

Press Previous (‹ or the left arrow key) to return to the main path.

Open Performance and record the click

Recordrepeat the click
Main trackflame chart
Red parttask over 50 ms
Bottom-upcostly function

Press Previous (‹ or the left arrow key) to return to the main path.

Deep dive: Slow clicks

Wrong first choice: Network

Performance first

  • Tasks on a timeline
  • Long tasks marked red
  • Interactions over 200 ms marked

Network first

  • Requests only
  • Busy main thread not shown
  • You may blame a fast request

Slow input is a main-thread problem until the trace says otherwise.

Deep dive: Memory grows

Name the memory symptom first

Symptom

  • Slower and slower over time
  • Bad from the start
  • Frequent short pauses

Likely problem

  • Memory leak
  • Memory bloat
  • Frequent garbage collection

Press Previous (‹ or the left arrow key) to return to the main path.

Deep dive: Memory grows

Compare two heap snapshots

Snapshot 1the baseline heap
Open and close the dialogthe action and its reverse
Snapshot 2the heap after
Comparison viewwhat grew, such as detached DOM nodes

Press Previous (‹ or the left arrow key) to return to the main path.

Deep dive: Memory grows

Wrong first choice: one snapshot

Two snapshots

  • Same action between them
  • Growth is visible
  • Retainers show who holds it

One snapshot

  • Size at one moment
  • Normal and leaked objects mixed
  • Growth stays hidden

A leak is a change over time, so measure twice.

Press Previous (‹ or the left arrow key) to return to the main path.

Deep dive: Broken layout

Open Elements and inspect the box

  1. 1Right-click the broken element, choose Inspect
  2. 2Read the Styles pane: which rules apply
  3. 3Crossed-out rules were overridden
  4. 4Edit a value live to test the fix

Press Previous (‹ or the left arrow key) to return to the main path.

Deep dive: Broken layout

Wrong first choice: Sources

Elements first

  • The element's box and rules
  • Overrides shown
  • Live edit tests a fix

Sources first

  • JavaScript line by line
  • CSS cause not shown
  • Slow path to the rule

Inspect the box before you debug the script.

Press Previous (‹ or the left arrow key) to return to the main path.

Deep dive: Stale data

Open Application, then Network

  1. 1Application, Service Workers: which worker is active
  2. 2Tick Update on reload or Bypass for network
  3. 3Application, Cache Storage: the cached responses
  4. 4Network, Disable cache: reload and compare

Press Previous (‹ or the left arrow key) to return to the main path.

Deep dive: Stale data

Wrong first choice: Elements

Application first

  • Service worker state
  • Cached responses listed
  • Source of the old value

Elements first

  • The old value on screen
  • No origin shown
  • You confirm, not explain

Find where the data came from, not only what it shows.

Press Previous (‹ or the left arrow key) to return to the main path.

Deep dive: Error only on iPhone

Attach Web Inspector to the real iPhone

  1. 1iPhone: Settings, Safari, Advanced, Web Inspector on
  2. 2Mac Safari: show features for web developers
  3. 3Connect the cable
  4. 4Develop menu: pick the iPhone and the page
  5. 5Read the error in the device's Console

Press Previous (‹ or the left arrow key) to return to the main path.

Deep dive: Error only on iPhone

Wrong first choice: device mode only

Real device

  • The phone's own browser
  • The real error and stack
  • Needs a cable and a Mac

Device mode

  • Desktop Chrome, small viewport
  • Fast to open
  • Can miss phone-only errors

Use device mode for layout; use the real device for a device-only error.
